If you have a backyard, you already have everything you need to start composting. Every week, most households throw away a surprising amount of food scraps: banana peels, coffee grounds, eggshells, wilted lettuce. Instead of sending all of that to the landfill, you can turn it into rich, dark soil that your garden will love.

Getting started is easier than it sounds. Pick a sunny or partly shaded corner of your yard, set up a simple bin or even just a pile, and start adding a mix of kitchen scraps and dry yard waste like fallen leaves, grass clippings, and small twigs. Turn the pile with a garden fork every week or two, keep it about as damp as a wrung-out sponge, and let nature do the rest. In a few months, you'll have free compost for your flower beds and vegetable patch.

In this series, we'll walk through choosing the right spot, what to add and what to skip, and how to fix common problems like bad smells or a pile that won't break down.

delivery:
Hearty Vegan Split Pea Soup

Serves 4 to 6

Ingredients
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 large yellow onion, diced
- 2 carrots, peeled and diced
- 2 celery stalks, diced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme
- 2 cups (about 400 g) dried green split peas, rinsed and picked over
- 1 can (14 oz / 400 g) diced tomatoes
- 7 cups vegetable broth
- 2 bay leaves
- 2 cups fresh spinach, roughly chopped
- 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- Chopped fresh parsley, for serving

Method
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, for 6 to 8 minutes until softened.
2. Stir in the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika and thyme and cook for about 1 minute, until fragrant.
3. Add the rinsed split peas, diced tomatoes with their juices, vegetable broth and bay leaves. Stir well and bring to a boil.
4. Reduce the heat to low, cover partially and simmer for 45 to 55 minutes, stirring now and then, until the split peas are completely tender and starting to break down. Add a splash more broth if the soup gets too thick.
5. Remove the bay leaves. For a creamier texture, blend about a third of the soup with an immersion blender, or leave it chunky if you prefer.
6. Stir in the spinach and let it wilt for 1 to 2 minutes, then add the lemon juice and season with salt and pepper. Ladle into bowls and top with chopped parsley.

Hearty Vegan Lentil Soup

Serves 4 to 6

Ingredients
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 medium yellow onion, diced
- 2 carrots, peeled and diced
- 2 celery stalks, diced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme
- 1 1/2 cups dried brown or green lentils, rinsed and picked over
- 1 can (14 oz) diced tomatoes, with their juices
- 6 cups low-sodium vegetable broth
- 1 bay leaf
- 2 cups fresh spinach or chopped kale
- 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- Chopped fresh parsley, for serving

Steps
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, for 6 to 8 minutes, until the vegetables are softened.
2. Stir in the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika and thyme, and cook for about 1 minute, until fragrant.
3. Add the rinsed lentils, diced tomatoes with their juices, vegetable broth and bay leaf. Stir well and bring to a boil.
4. Reduce the heat to low, partially cover, and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are tender. Add a splash of water if the soup gets too thick.
5. Remove the bay leaf. For a creamier texture, blend about a third of the soup with an immersion blender, or transfer 2 cups to a blender, purée, and return it to the pot. Stir in the spinach or kale and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until wilted.
6. Stir in the lemon juice, season with salt and pepper to taste, and ladle into bowls. Garnish with chopped parsley and serve hot.

Boxing
Learn to jab, cross, hook and uppercut in this pad-based class. Partner drills sharpen your technique, while bursts of conditioning build power and stamina. No sparring and no experience needed. The class lasts 45 minutes. Gloves are available to borrow, but wraps are recommended.

Pilates
Build core strength and better posture with controlled, precise mat-based movements. This class focuses on stability, alignment and breathing, helping to support your back and improve everyday movement. Beginners are welcome, with modifications for every exercise. The class lasts 45 minutes.

Stretch
